title: Fresh Pond Site
summary: Fresh Pond on Shelter Island is associated with archaeological evidence of shellfish processing, tools, pottery, fire-cracked rock, and repeated seasonal or year-round occupation. Its specific archaeological deposits are not publicly identified.
address_label: Fresh Pond, Shelter Island, New York (approximate public area)
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Manhansett Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: The extensive archaeological discovery of fire-cracked rocks, domestic pottery, and dense shellfish refuse pits at the Fresh Pond Site indicates that this location served as a permanent, year-round residential base camp. Recognizing such complex, long-term settlements challenges the misconception that early Indigenous communities were purely nomadic, revealing instead how they established deeply rooted, sustainable villages on Shelter Island.
